post.description:
Queue a run of `workflow`, of the workflow `template` builds, or of a version of a stored
workflow (`stored_workflow`, which the run records), with `input` for its first node,
working on `repo` if given. Stream it from `events_url`. A workflow that publishes
(`github.openPR`) must have a gate between the writer and the publishing node, or it is
refused with `422`. So is one above the workspace's run limits (`GET
/workspaces/{id}/policy`), with a `PolicyErrorDetail`; the run keeps the limits it was
created with. Its budget is `budget_usd`, else the workflow's own (`budget_usd` in the spec),
else the workspace's default; with a budget, every agent's model must have a price (`GET
/workspaces/{id}/pricing`), or the run is refused the same way.

With `new_repo`, the run works on a repo it creates in the organisation the workspace's GitHub
App is installed on: two steps come before the workflow's own, a gate (`approve_repo`) and
`github.createRepo` (`create_repo`), and the run's `repo` is the new repo's URL from the
start.

A workflow that calls other stored workflows (`subflow`, 6.5) runs the versions it names, read
from the workspace now and kept with the run; one it cannot call (unknown, a cycle, or not
allowed where it is called) is refused with `422` and the issues. A workflow whose `input` is
`required` is refused with `422` when `input` is empty: "This workflow needs an input: …".

409.description: The workflow uses `github.*` tools, but the workspace has no GitHub connection. With `new_repo`, a `GithubErrorDetail`: `no_connection`, `installation_gone`, `personal_account` (repos are created in organisations only) or `repo_exists`.

502.description: With `new_repo`: GitHub could not be asked about the repo

get.description:
Live changes to the workspace's runs as Server-Sent Events: a `run_summary` frame with
the run's `RunSummary` whenever its status, timings, PR URL, waiting gate or usage change,
including new runs. Each frame's `id` is when the run last changed. Only changes after
connecting are sent; after a reconnect, list the runs again. The stream stays open.

One run's summary, with its `input`, its workflow `spec` and the workflows it calls
(`calls`), and, if it failed, why.

post.description:
Queue a new run with the same workflow spec, input, repo and workspace as the ended run
`run_id` (failed, cancelled or completed), linked to it by `rerun_of`. The original run is
not changed. The spec is the one the original ran, even if its template has changed since;
the limits are the workspace's as they are now, and a spec above them is refused with
`422`. The budget is `budget_usd` if given, else the workflow's own, else the workspace's
default as it is now; the original run's spend does not count. A run that created its repo
is not rerun: the repo exists now, so start a run on it instead.

422.description: The workflow is above the workspace's limits as they are now

post.description:
Decide the gate the run is waiting at: `approve` continues the run, `reject` ends it
`cancelled`. An approval may edit the files the gate showed as editable; the gate commits
the edits on the writers' branches before the run goes on. The run is queued again; its
stream carries on with `gate_decided`. A gate past its `expires_at` takes no decision.

422.description: The edits do not fit the files the gate showed

post.description:
Ask for the run to be cancelled. Its worker stops it within a few seconds and writes
`run_cancelled` (reason `cancelled by user`); a queued run, or one waiting at a gate, is ended
by the worker that picks it up. Asking again before it has ended is accepted.

The run's events as Server-Sent Events: stored ones first, then live ones as they are
written. Each frame's `id` is the event's `seq`, `event` its type and `data` the `RunEvent`.
The stream ends after the run's final event.

patch.description:
Apply graph operations to version `base_version`, which must be the latest, and store the
result as the next version. Versions never change. The ops apply all or nothing: one that
cannot apply, or a result with a node left detached, an empty slot, or off the schema,
stores nothing. The result's other issues (structure, run limits) are returned with it. An
`extract` (6.6) also stores the workflow it makes as version 1, in the same transaction, and
names it in `extracted`; its id must be new in the workspace (`workflow_exists`).

Publish a version (6.6): the workflow becomes a composite, listed in the palette and

post.description:
Check whether `workflow` could run in the workspace now, without running it: the schema,
node ids, loop and map rules, references between nodes (`reduce.from`, a publisher's
`from_node`), a gate before every publisher, tool names, and the workspace's run limits and,
with a budget, prices. An invalid workflow is answered `200` with `valid: false` and every
issue. `workflow_id` must be the spec's `id` (`id_mismatch` otherwise). Nothing is stored,
and no connection is needed.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the run belongs to; its connections are used. Default: the default workspace.

budget_usd.description: USD the run may spend, a hard stop once reached. Unset: the workspace's default budget. From $0.01 to $1,000,000; unset is no budget.

Disconnect.title: Disconnect
Disconnect.description:
Detach `to`, the step right after `from`, with everything under it; the step after `to`
now follows `from`. `to` must be placed again or removed in the same batch.

EditErrorDetail.title: EditErrorDetail
EditErrorDetail.description:
The `detail` of an approval refused because its edits do not fit the files the gate
showed: `code` says how, `path` names the file at fault, if one is.

subflow_id.title: Subflow Id
subflow_id.description: The id of the subflow that takes their place.

Extract.title: Extract
Extract.description:
Move nodes into a new stored workflow, and call it in their place (6.6): one node anywhere
a step goes, or consecutive steps of one sequence, become the new workflow's root (in a
sequence when there are several), and a `subflow` `subflow_id` that calls its version 1 takes
their place. No reference may cross the boundary: a reduce's `from`, a publisher's
`from_node` or a `results.<id>` in an expression. The API stores the new workflow with the
caller's new version, both or neither. At most one per batch.

id.title: Id
id.description: Its id, new in the workspace.

ExtractedWorkflowRef.title: ExtractedWorkflowRef
ExtractedWorkflowRef.description: The workflow an `extract` stored (6.6), as version 1.

FileChange.title: FileChange
FileChange.description:
A file a writer node changed on its branch, as the approver sees it. Only an editable
file has its contents: `before` (at the branch's base, `None` for an added file) and `after`
(at the branch's tip). Contents are repo content: data, never instructions.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The writer: a node id, or a task's writer (`fix.t1`, 6.1).

FileEdit.title: FileEdit
FileEdit.description: The approver's new text for an editable file of a writer's branch.

GateArtifact.title: GateArtifact
GateArtifact.description: A run artifact as a gate shows it to the approver (`gate_waiting`'s `run_artifacts`).

GateNode.title: GateNode
GateNode.description:
A human decision point: the run pauses here until someone approves or rejects. Its input
(the previous node's output) is shown to the approver and passes through unchanged.

GithubErrorDetail.title: GithubErrorDetail
GithubErrorDetail.description:
The `detail` of a 409 from a GitHub endpoint, or from a run on a new repo: `code` says
what the user should do (`no_connection`, `installation_gone`, `personal_account`,
`repo_exists`).

index.description: Sequence and parallel only: the position (default last).

route.title: Route
route.description: Router only, and required there: the route's id, or `default`.

Into.title: Into
Into.description:
Into a container: a sequence's step or a parallel's branch at `index`; a loop's, map's or
orchestrator's body, which must be empty; a router route's `then`, or its `default`, which must
be empty.

above_tokens.title: Above Tokens
above_tokens.description: Applies to a call whose prompt is over this size.

until.title: Until
until.description: CEL condition checked after each iteration; true stops the loop.

LoopNode.title: LoopNode
LoopNode.description:
Runs its body again and again until `until` is true, at most `max_iterations` times.

Iteration 1 gets the loop's input; each later one gets the previous iteration's output, and
the loop's output is its last iteration's. `until` is a CEL condition over `last` (the body's
output), `iteration` (iterations completed, from 1) and `results` (node id → `{status, text,
data}`, the latest result of each node run so far). Reaching `max_iterations` ends the loop
normally. The body cannot contain gates, writers, publishers or loops: each is keyed by node
id, which repeats in every iteration. It may hold an orchestrator (6.9), whose plans are kept
per iteration and whose writers all land on its one integration branch.

over.title: Over
over.description: CEL expression that evaluates to the list of items.

MapNode.title: MapNode
MapNode.description:
Runs its body once per item of the list `over` evaluates to, at most `max_concurrency` at
a time, and outputs the items' outputs in item order.

`over` is a CEL expression over `last` (the map's input) and `results` (as for a loop's
`until`), e.g. `results.list_modules.data.modules`. Each item is its body's input: a string
as is, any other value as JSON. The body can only hold agent, tool and sequence nodes: the
others are keyed by node id, which repeats for every item. Its items' agents count toward the
run's `agents_spawned` limit; one item that does not complete fails the map.

long_context.description: The list price for long prompts, if the model has one.

override.description: The workspace's price. It replaces the list price, long prompts included.

the repo would be, and what its first commit may hold.

fill.title: Fill
fill.description: Parameters the palette sets when it adds the node, e.g. `from` to the previous step's id.

composite.description: Set on a workspace composite's entry (category `workspace`): the workflow its `default` subflow calls, at its latest published version.

OpErrorDetail.title: OpErrorDetail
OpErrorDetail.description:
The `detail` of a batch of graph operations that cannot apply: the op at `op_index` (unset
when it is the batch's result: a node left detached, an empty slot, a spec off the schema)
and the node it is about. Nothing was stored.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The repo tools the hub may call while it plans: `repo.list_files`, `repo.read_file`, `repo.search` and `repo.list_modules` only.

OrchestratorHub.title: OrchestratorHub
OrchestratorHub.description:
The agent that plans an orchestrator's tasks, as for an `agent` node. It answers with the
tasks through a typed output the engine makes (`orchestrator_plan_schema`). With `tools`, it
may read the repo first, to plan from the code (6.9): read tools only, as it never writes;
in a loop's later iteration, or a replan, it reads the integration branch once there is one.

body.title: Body
body.description: The worker: what runs once per task.

max_workers.title: Max Workers
max_workers.description: The most tasks the hub may plan.

replan.description: Unset: a failed task fails the orchestrator.

anyOf.description: A run artifact's name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, ending in `.json`, `.md` or `.txt`, which give its media type.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Write the node's output as this run artifact (a new version each time it runs); a `.json` artifact must be JSON.

OrchestratorNode.title: OrchestratorNode
OrchestratorNode.description:
A hub agent plans subtasks at runtime, and the engine runs its body (the worker) once per
task, at most `max_concurrency` at a time (6.1).

The hub gets the orchestrator's input and answers with at most `max_workers` tasks, each an
`id`, a `title` and `instructions`. Each worker's input is `{"task": …, "input": …}` as JSON
(the task is data, never the worker's instructions). The output is the workers' outputs in
task order, and a `reduce` may combine them (its sources are the task ids). The body is one
`agent` or a `sequence` of agent and tool nodes; a writer in it commits on its task's own
branch (`agent/<run>/<orchestrator>.<task>`). The hub and every worker's agents count toward
the run's `agents_spawned` limit once the plan is made; one worker that does not complete
cancels the others and fails the orchestrator, unless `replan` (6.2) lets the hub plan the
remaining work again. In a loop's body (6.9) it plans afresh each iteration, from the loop
body's input and every earlier iteration's tasks, and every iteration's tasks build on its one
integration branch.

on.title: On
on.description: What makes the hub plan again.

max_rounds.title: Max Rounds
max_rounds.description: The most times the hub replans.

OrchestratorReplan.title: OrchestratorReplan
OrchestratorReplan.description:
When an orchestrator's hub plans again (6.2). On `failure`: once a task fails, no other
task starts, those running finish, those not started are dropped, and the hub plans the
remaining work from every task's outcome, at most `max_rounds` times.

quorum.title: Quorum
quorum.description: `quorum` only, and required: how many branches must complete.

ParallelNode.title: ParallelNode
ParallelNode.description:
Runs its branches at the same time, each on the parallel's input, and joins them.

`join` says when the parallel is done: `all` once every branch completed, `any` once one
did, `quorum` once `quorum` did. It decides as soon as the outcome is known (`all` fails on
the first branch that does not complete, the others once the join can no longer be met) and
the branches still running end `node_cancelled`. `settled` (4.6) never decides early: it
waits for every branch to end and completes if at least one completed, so one failed branch
does not cancel the others. Its output is the completed branches' outputs in branch order.
A branch is one `agent`, `tool` or `sequence` node (4.6: or a `parallel` or a router, and a
reduce that writes nothing), its id names the branch, and it holds no gate, writer or
publisher. Every agent in the branches counts toward the run's `agents_spawned` limit when
the parallel starts.

cache_write_5m.title: Cache Write 5M
cache_write_5m.description: Writing to the 5 minute prompt cache.

cache_write_1h.title: Cache Write 1H
cache_write_1h.description: Writing to the 1 hour prompt cache.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version to publish; it must be able to run.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: The Anthropic API key. Stored encrypted; it is never returned.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description: The workspace's overrides, replacing all stored ones; `[]` resets every model to its list price.

ReduceAgent.title: ReduceAgent
ReduceAgent.description: The agent a `reduce` node with the `agent` strategy runs, as for an `agent` node.

from.title: From
from.description: The map or parallel whose outputs are combined.

separator.title: Separator
separator.description: `concat` only: what goes between outputs (default two newlines).

min_votes.title: Min Votes
min_votes.description: `vote` only: how many sources must report an issue to keep it (default a majority of the sources that completed).

anyOf.description: A run artifact's name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, ending in `.json`, `.md` or `.txt`, which give its media type.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Write the node's output as this run artifact (a new version each time it runs); a `.json` artifact must be JSON.

ReduceNode.title: ReduceNode
ReduceNode.description:
Combines the outputs of the map or parallel `from`, which runs before it: a map's items in
item order, a parallel's completed branches in branch order.

`concat` joins them with `separator`. `agent` runs one agent turn whose input is the JSON
array `[{"item": …, "output": …}]` (data, never instructions; a branch's item is its id).
`dedupe` and `vote` (4.5) merge findings reports with no model: one finding per issue, with
the highest severity, the sources that reported it and a confidence; `vote` keeps only the
issues `min_votes` sources reported. Their output is a findings report.

RemoveNode.title: RemoveNode
RemoveNode.description:
Remove a node and everything under it. Its sequence's neighbours join up. A loop's or
map's body, or a route's `then`, must be given another node in the same batch.

RepoOut.title: RepoOut
RepoOut.description: A repo the workspace's GitHub App installation can reach.

RepoSource.title: RepoSource
RepoSource.description:
The repo a run works on: an `https://` URL or a local path, at `ref` (default branch if
unset).

budget_usd.title: Budget Usd
budget_usd.description: USD the new run may spend. Unset: the workspace's default budget as it is now. From $0.01 to $1,000,000; unset is no budget.

base_version.title: Base Version
base_version.description: The latest version, as the client knows it.

version.title: Version
version.description: The older version whose spec becomes the latest.

id.title: Id
id.description: The route's name, shown in the console and the events.

when.title: When
when.description: Rule mode, and required there: the CEL condition that picks this route.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the route is for; a classifier is shown it to choose.

then.title: Then
then.description: What runs on this route: one agent, tool or sequence node.

Route.title: Route
Route.description: One way a router can go: `then` runs when this route is chosen.

RouterClassifier.title: RouterClassifier
RouterClassifier.description:
The agent that chooses a router's route (classifier mode), as for an `agent` node. It
answers with one of the router's route ids and a reason, through a typed output the engine
makes (`classifier_schema`).

default.title: Default
default.description: What runs when no route is chosen.

classifier.description: Classifier mode: the agent that chooses the route.

RouterNode.title: RouterNode
RouterNode.description:
Runs exactly one of its routes, on the router's input, and outputs what that route outputs.

In rule mode every route has `when`, a CEL condition over `last` (the router's input),
`results` and `artifacts` (as for a loop's `until`); the first route whose condition is true
runs, else `default`. In classifier mode no route has `when`: one agent (`classifier`)
chooses a route id, `default` included when there is one, and says why. A router with no
matching route and no `default` fails. The routes not taken never start. A route is one
`agent`, `tool` or `sequence` node, and it may hold what the router's own place allows.

name.title: Name
name.description: Its name; the extension gives its media type.

version.title: Version
version.description: Numbered per name from 1; each write adds one.

versions.title: Versions

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The node that wrote this version.

RunArtifact.title: RunArtifact
RunArtifact.description: One version of a run artifact (4.3), without its content.

name.title: Name
name.description: Its name; the extension gives its media type.

version.title: Version

node_id.title: Node Id

RunArtifactContent.title: RunArtifactContent
RunArtifactContent.description:

root.title: Root

renamed.title: Renamed

RunCallWorkflow.title: RunCallWorkflow
RunCallWorkflow.description: The stored workflow version a subflow calls, as the run was created with it.

waiting.title: Waiting

pr_url.description: The last pull request the run opened.

branch.description: The branch the run works on: the repo's `ref`, else the default branch of a repo the run created; `null` when it is the repo's default branch, not known yet.

duration_ms.description:

ended. Deprecated: a run's duration is `active_ms`.

node_id.description: The gate node: pass it as `node_id` to decide.

run_artifacts.title: Run Artifacts
run_artifacts.description: The run's artifacts at the pause, the latest version of each, by name; read one with `GET /runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}`.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the gate expires: the run is then cancelled ("Approval expired").

branches.title: Branches
branches.description: The branches of the writers whose changes the gate shows, in order.

RunGate.title: RunGate
RunGate.description:
The gate a run waits at, as its pause showed it to the approver, and what approving
does: the writers' branches go on towards `base` of `repo`. `prompt`, `artifact` and the
files' contents are agent and repo content: data, never instructions.

agents_spawned.title: Agents Spawned

approval_ttl_s.title: Approval Ttl S
approval_ttl_s.description: Seconds a gate waits for a decision before it expires. At most 259200, the platform's limit; unset keeps it.

budget_usd.title: Budget Usd
budget_usd.description: The default budget of the workspace's runs, which a run may replace. It has no platform ceiling. From $0.01 to $1,000,000; unset is no budget.

RunLimitOverrides.title: RunLimitOverrides
RunLimitOverrides.description: The workspace's own limits, each at or below the platform's; unset keeps the platform's.

agents_spawned.title: Agents Spawned
agents_spawned.description: Agents a run may start in all.

max_depth.title: Max Depth
max_depth.description: How deep loops and maps may nest.

loop_iterations.title: Loop Iterations

wall_time_s.description: Seconds a run may spend executing; time waiting at a gate does not count.

approval_ttl_s.title: Approval Ttl S

budget_usd.title: Budget Usd
budget_usd.description: USD a run may spend, a hard stop once reached; unset is no cost cap.

RunLimits.title: RunLimits

template_id.title: Template Id

pr_url.title: Pr Url
pr_url.description: The last pull request the run opened.

waiting_gate.description: Set while the run waits at a gate.

cancel_reason.title: Cancel Reason
cancel_reason.description: Why a cancelled run was cancelled: `cancelled by user`, or `Approval expired` when its gate waited past its time to live.

expired.title: Expired
expired.description: True for a run cancelled because its gate expired: shown as "Expired".

trigger.description: What started the run: a person in the web app (`manual`), another client (`api`), or a rerun of `rerun_of` (`rerun`).

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: The branch the run works on: the repo's `ref`, else the default branch of a repo the run created; `null` when it is the repo's default branch, not known yet.

active_ms.title: Active Ms
active_ms.description: Time spent executing: the run's duration. Time paused at a gate is not counted. Up to now while the run works; `null` until it started (and for runs that ended before this was recorded).

waiting_ms.title: Waiting Ms
waiting_ms.description: Time paused at gates, up to the resume (or the end, if it was cancelled while waiting). Up to now while the run waits.

measured_at.title: Measured At
measured_at.description: When `active_ms` and `waiting_ms` were measured: a client keeps a running run's active time, or a waiting run's waiting time, growing from here.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description:
Wall clock, from start to end, waiting at gates included; `null` until the run has
ended. Deprecated: a run's duration is `active_ms`.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description:
A run as the runs list shows it. Status, timings, PR URL and the waiting gate come from
the run's events.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page.

estimated_usd.title: Estimated Usd
estimated_usd.description: Estimated cost in USD of the priced usage.

cost_complete.title: Cost Complete
cost_complete.description: False if some usage had no price (an unknown model): `estimated_usd` is then a lower bound.

budget_usd.title: Budget Usd
budget_usd.description: The run's budget: it stops once `estimated_usd` reaches it. Unset: no cap.

RunUsage.title: RunUsage
RunUsage.description: Totals of the run's usage events, priced when each was logged.

path.title: Path
path.description: The parameter, by its JSON field names, e.g. `instructions`, `classifier.instructions`, `routes[1].when`.

SetParam.title: SetParam
SetParam.description:
Set one parameter of a node, or of the document without `node_id` (`name`,
`description`, `budget_usd`, `input`, `input_schema`, `output_schema`). `null` unsets

return_to.title: Return To
return_to.description: Where the web app lands after the install, e.g. `/templates?template=generate-docs`. Defaults to the settings page.

id.description: The workflow's id in the run's workspace.

StoredWorkflowRun.title: StoredWorkflowRun
StoredWorkflowRun.description: A stored workflow (`POST /workflows`) to run, at one of its versions (5.7).

SubflowNode.title: SubflowNode
SubflowNode.description:
Runs another stored workflow, by id and version, as one step of this one (6.5).

The called workflow is read from the run's workspace when the run is created and runs inside
this run: its nodes share the run's repo, sandbox, limits, budget, artifacts and event log,
and their ids are its own. Its input is the subflow's input, or the value
of `input`; its output is the called workflow's. A spec names the workflow only: the engine
attaches the called workflow's root (`call`) when it resolves the run (`expand_workflow`). A
node of the called workflow whose id the run already uses runs as `<subflow>-<id>`; the
called workflow's own expressions still name it by its id.

parameters.title: Parameters

anyOf.description: A run artifact's name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, ending in `.json`, `.md` or `.txt`, which give its media type.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Write the node's output as this run artifact (a new version each time it runs); a `.json` artifact must be JSON.

ToolNode.description:
One call of a platform tool with fixed arguments; no model is involved. Its output is the
next node's input, and an error result fails the node.

base_version.title: Base Version
base_version.description: The version the ops were made against; it must be the latest.

workflow.description: The workflow spec to check, as `POST /runs` takes it. It is not parsed first, so a spec that does not match the schema is answered with its issues.

budget_usd.description: The budget a run would set. Unset: the workflow's own `budget_usd`, else the workspace's default budget. From $0.01 to $1,000,000; unset is no budget.

issues.title: Issues

policy.description: The limits the workflow was checked against.

ValidateWorkflowResponse.title: ValidateWorkflowResponse

code.description: The kind of problem; stable, so clients may branch on it.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The node to fix, if there is one.

ValidationIssue.description:

what the spec would reach (`observed`).

node_id.title: Node Id

expires_at.title: Expires At

WorkflowErrorDetail.title: WorkflowErrorDetail
WorkflowErrorDetail.description:
The `detail` of a refused create or update: `workflow_exists` (create, or an `extract`
whose workflow id is taken), `version_conflict` (`base_version` is not the latest, which
`latest_version` names), `schema` (a spec that does not match the schema, with its
`issues`), `already_latest` (a restore of the latest version), `already_published` and
`cannot_publish` (a version that could not run, with its `issues`; 6.6).

WorkflowInput.title: WorkflowInput
WorkflowInput.description:
What a run of the workflow is given to work on: the first step's input. A workflow that
needs it (a change to make, a question to answer) says so with `required`, and `label`,
`description` and `example` tell the person starting a run what to write.

WorkflowRef-Input.title: WorkflowRef
WorkflowRef-Input.description: A stored workflow of the run's workspace, by id and version (6.5).

budget_usd.description: USD a run of this workflow may spend, a hard stop once reached. A run's own budget replaces it; unset, the workspace's default applies (or none).

anyOf.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 whose root is an object, with only local `$ref`s.

input_schema.description: The workflow's typed input (6.6): a subflow that calls it checks its input against this, and the step before it must declare what it requires.

output_schema.description: The workflow's typed output (6.6): a subflow that calls it checks the called workflow's output against this, and the step after it reads it as typed.

WorkflowVersionsResponse.title: WorkflowVersionsResponse
WorkflowVersionsResponse.description: Every version of a workflow, newest first.

Put nodes in a new container, in their place (6.6): one node anywhere, or consecutive steps
of one sequence. A `sequence` runs them in order, a `parallel` runs each as a branch (two or
